extracted.intended_audience: SAG-AFTRA members, performers, and entertainment industry readers/interested public
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the union's strike rules describing what work members may not perform during the SAG-AFTRA strike, including specific categories of services, procedural instructions for members/agents, exceptions, and penalties for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the strike rules (covered services withheld)
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidelines govern the work the union's members are allowed and not allowed to perform during a potential labor action targeting film and television companies; all covered services and performing work must be withheld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to SAG-AFTRA's roughly 160,000 affected members; the strike begins at midnight and will lead to immediate shutdowns of major film shoots. The bulletin frames the list as 'including but not limited to,' so the listed items are illustrative, not necessarily exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal on-camera work prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Members are prohibited from performing principal on-camera work during the strike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples enumerated: Acting; Singing; Dancing; Performing stunts; Piloting on-camera aircraft; Puppeteering; Performance capture or motion capture work. These are explicit examples of principal on-camera covered services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal off-camera work prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Members are prohibited from performing principal off-camera work that constitutes covered services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed: ADR/Looping; TV trailers (promos) and theatrical trailers; Voice acting; Singing; Narration; Stunt coordinating and related services; Stand-in work; Photo and/or body doubles; Fittings, wardrobe tests, and makeup tests; Rehearsals and camera tests; Scanning; Interviews and auditions (including via self-tape). The bulletin groups many production-support activities as covered services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background and stand-in work prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Background (extras) work and stand-in work are barred under the strike rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned in article prose and listed among off-camera services; treated as covered services members must withhold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion and publicity services prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Members are barred from promotional or publicity activities for work under the TV/Theatrical Contracts while the strike is in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit items include: Tours; Personal appearances; Interviews; Conventions; Fan expos; Festivals; 'For your consideration' events; Panels; Premieres/screenings; Award shows; Junkets; Podcast appearances; Social media; Studio showcases. The article cites red carpet appearances, festival appearances (Venice, Toronto, Galway), Fan events at Comic-Con, and FYC campaigns as examples of barred publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiating/entering into/consenting to future agreements prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Members must not negotiate, enter into, or consent to agreements to perform covered services for struck companies during the strike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sub-items called out: Any agreement to perform covered services in the future; Any new agreement related to merchandising connected to a covered project; The creation and use of digital replicas, including through reuse of prior work. The notice instructs members to direct agents to cease all negotiations for services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation/use of digital replicas and reuse of prior work restricted
rubrics_metrics.description: The creation and use of digital replicas (including reuse of prior work) for struck projects is prohibited without authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under the negotiating/consenting prohibition: the bulletin explicitly disallows consenting to creation/use of digital replicas as part of prohibited agreements. The article notes AI/digital likeness regulation as one of the union's bargaining priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performing on trailers or ancillary content connected to struck productions prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Members may not perform on a trailer for a struck production or other ancillary content connected to a struck production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is singled out as a prohibited act even when the primary project is struck; performing for ancillary/promotional material tied to a struck production is barred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditions, rehearsals, fittings, and camera tests barred
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditions, rehearsals, fittings, wardrobe/makeup tests, camera tests and similar preparatory activities are prohibited during the strike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bulletin lists auditions (including self-tape), rehearsals, fittings, wardrobe tests, makeup tests and camera tests among services members must withhold; the article emphasizes these as barred even if not final on-camera performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Members must direct agents to cease negotiations and report strikebreaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The strike notice instructs members to direct their agents to cease all negotiations for services and to inform the union of any strikebreaking activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural requirement: members are expected to ensure representatives stop negotiating deals and to report any attempts at strikebreaking so the union can act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Agreement exception for non-AMPTP productions
rubrics_metrics.description: Members may be able to work on projects produced by non-AMPTP-related production companies if such projects qualify for an Interim Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bulletin says a list of eligible projects will be posted on the union website. This is an exception to the general prohibitions and requires an Interim Agreement to be in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty/warning for nonmembers who perform covered services
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonmembers who perform covered services for a struck company may be barred from future union admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice warns nonmembers they won't be admitted into the union in the future if they perform covered services for a struck company during the strike—this functions as a deterrent/penalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity-specific examples illustrating scope (red carpets, festivals, FYC campaigns)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules specifically bar promotional activity such as walking red carpets, attending premieres/festivals, participating in FYC campaigns and other high-profile publicity events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites Universal moving a red carpet earlier to allow cast photocalls before a strike announcement, and mentions Venice, Toronto, Galway, Comic-Con, and 'For Your Consideration' campaigns as concrete examples of barred activity—useful for interpreting the breadth of 'publicity services.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual bargaining goals referenced (residuals, AI, virtual auditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The union's bargaining priorities shape the rules: higher compensation/residuals, reworking streaming residuals, regulating generative AI and restrictions on virtual auditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not a prohibition itself, the article frames many of the strike rules and the digital-replica prohibition in the context of these bargaining objectives; this contextual guidance explains why certain items (AI/digital likenesses, virtual auditions) are emphasized.
